english.title: Retain official document when no right / contrary to duty to do so
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[retained for a purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFICIAL DOCUMENT..), when you had no right to retain it]_
(B)_[retained for a purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFICIAL DOCUMENT..), when it was contrary to your duty to retain it]_
(C)_[failed to comply with a direction, namely **(..SPECIFY DIRECTION..), issued by a Government Department, namely **(..SPECIFY DEPARTMENT..), or a person authorised by that Department, with regard to the return or disposal of an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(2)(a) and 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.

english.notes:
(i) Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).
(ii) An official document is a passport or a naval, military, air-force, police, or official pass, permit, certificate, licence or other document of a similar character

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
